Better Facial Animations - GPU setup and recovery

The installer has a short recovery page. Keep this full guide for troubleshooting
without having to launch Skyrim. No helper program is launched by this version.

[Requirements and drivers]

Independent GPU + V3 is the normal preset. V3 tries GPU inference after a save loads or a
new game starts. Early dialogue keeps vanilla animation while the model warms
up. A returned GPU failure can be retried with Try GPU again.
Shared GPU retries without metacommands, then conditionally through an observed
graphics wrapper after device loss. Further shared attempts wait 2/4/8/16/30 seconds;
sentiment retries after 30 seconds. GPU failures never automatically select CPU.
ForceCPU explicitly uses your chosen model on CPU. Performance has less facial detail than V3.

The installer has three independent choices:
- GPU route: Standard (independent, recommended), or Compatibility (4.0-style
  shared). Shared is available for Deck/older runtimes or as a deliberate test
  after independent-device black screens/CTDs. It can also cause conflicts;
  do not assume it is safer just because your GPU is older.
- First launch: start with GPU after loading, or Force CPU. CPU startup
  sets ForceCPU=1 and preserves your selected GPU route for later opt-in.
  It stays on until you change it; the second launch does not enable GPU.
- Starting settings: choose V3 for detail, Performance for speed, or Old for
  its facial style and lower VRAM use than V3. Separate checkboxes control
  Potato Mode, player animation and early dialogue preparation.
  These can all be changed in game with SKSE Menu Framework; no reinstall
  is needed. Speaker coverage is independent of model and GPU/CPU startup.

Model hardware estimates (additional to Skyrim, not total graphics memory):
- V3: roughly 250 MB device allocations; budget about 300 MB with runtime.
  Main network arithmetic: about 28 GFLOP per second of generated speech.
- Performance: roughly 80 MB with runtime; budget about 100 MB.
  Main network arithmetic: about 0.007 GFLOP per second of generated speech.
- Old: roughly 100 MB device allocations; budget about 150 MB with runtime.
  Main network arithmetic: about 97 GFLOP per second of generated speech.

All figures are rough. Local standalone RTX 4070 / Wine tests observed warmed
process footprints of about 278 / 77 / 128 MiB respectively. They exclude the
game and graphics mods and are not exhaustive startup-peak measurements.
Arithmetic estimates count multiply/add work in convolution, matrix and
recurrent layers, not frontend/mesh/driver costs. Short lines also incur
padding and startup context. GFLOP per second of speech is not the same as a
minimum GPU's advertised TFLOPS or a promise of ready-at-speech-start timing.

Provisional starting tiers to TRY, not benchmarked minimum cards:
V3: 4-6 TFLOPS FP32 (GTX 1660 class); Performance: 1-2 TFLOPS FP32
(GTX 1630 class); Old: 8-12 TFLOPS FP32 (RTX 2070 Super class).
These are broad planning heuristics, not measured cutoffs or purchase advice.
Equivalent AMD/Intel hardware may work; architecture, bandwidth and runtime
support matter as well as the advertised arithmetic rate. BFA competes with
Skyrim for GPU compute, memory and bandwidth. Heavier graphics mods leave less
capacity and can delay facial animation, even on a card above these tiers.

Steam Deck's published GPU rate is up to 1.6 TFLOPS FP32. The current Thin120
Performance model is a plausible compute fit and passes local GPU inference
on both routes, but has not been validated on Deck. The community's earlier
GPU success was with Thin96, so it does not confirm the current model.
Card comparison specifications and Deck specifications:
https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce/graphics-cards/compare/
https://www.steamdeck.com/en/tech

Independent GPU is recommended with RenoDX + DLSS 5, ReShade, and graphics
interactions involving Bottled/Open/Community Shaders, neural rendering,
upscaling or frame generation. Reports are not limited to one combination,
and neither route is a guaranteed fix for every setup.

Windows: both GPU routes need DirectX 12 hardware and a supporting driver.
Independent mode additionally needs the D3D12 Independent Devices API in
Windows, AND a driver that can actually create a separate device. Seeing
"DirectX 12" in dxdiag does not establish independent-device support.
Use Windows Update and restart. Microsoft introduced the API in the August
2023 updates for Windows 10 22H2 (KB5029331, build 19045.3393) and Windows 11
22H2 (KB5029351, build 22621.2215). These identify the API's arrival, not a
tested BFA minimum or a recommendation to install an old preview update.
Use current cumulative updates available for your Windows version. Check
your installed version with Start -> type "winver" -> Enter.

Install the current stable driver supported for your exact GPU and Windows
version from NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, or your laptop manufacturer's support page,
then restart. An old card may only have a legacy driver branch. There is no
verified minimum NVIDIA/AMD/Intel driver number or card-generation cutoff for
this mod's independent-device path; updating does not guarantee success.
On a laptop, check both integrated and discrete GPU drivers. Check BFA's log
for the adapter it actually selected; more VRAM on another adapter does not
mean it was selected. The mod does not yet guarantee matching Skyrim's GPU.

Official driver downloads:
NVIDIA: https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/drivers/
AMD: https://www.amd.com/en/support/download/drivers.html
Intel: https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/download-center/home.html

BFA uses DirectML, including on AMD and Intel; CUDA, Python, and an NVIDIA GPU
are not requirements. Keep this release's bundled DirectML/ONNX Runtime DLLs
and models together. Reinstall the complete package if files are missing or
mixed. Do not replace Windows system DLLs to try to add independent devices.
Leave GPU memory available beyond Skyrim's textures, upscaler and frame
generation. The model's usual memory use is not its maximum startup demand.

SteamOS / Steam Deck / Linux: GPU support depends on Proton and the Linux
GPU driver. A Deck user reported Performance + Potato working on GPU in the
4.0 era. This is evidence to offer the older shared route, not proof that
an independent device worked on that Deck. Try Compatibility GPU + Performance
+ Potato if independent mode is unsupported, or choose Force CPU first.
The shared route does not require Independent Devices support. It restores
4.2.1's metacommand/wrapper recovery and delayed shared GPU retries, with newer
delayed startup. It never probes or automatically selects independent mode.

For independent GPU, update SteamOS (or your distro's graphics stack) and use
a Proton build whose bundled vkd3d-proton supports Independent Devices.
Upstream lists this in 3.0.1; backports may also work. A Proton/GE version
number alone does not prove support. No exact Proton + Deck combination is
certified by this candidate. Updating does not guarantee a fix.
References for DirectML, the Windows API and Linux support:
https://onnxruntime.ai/docs/execution-providers/DirectML-ExecutionProvider.html
https://microsoft.github.io/DirectX-Specs/d3d/IndependentDevices.html
https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/servicing/os/windows-10/2023/08/august-22-2023-kb5029331-os-build-19045-3393-preview
https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/servicing/os/windows-11/2023/08/august-22-2023-kb5029351-os-build-22621-2215-preview
https://github.com/HansKristian-Work/vkd3d-proton/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md

[Recover from a black screen, freeze or crash]

1. Fully close Skyrim. Save a copy of BetterFacialAnimations.log and any
   Crash Logger / Freeze Logger output before another launch replaces it.

2. Reinstall this package and choose "Force CPU", then "Performance" and check
   "Potato Mode" for lower CPU work. Either GPU route can remain selected for later
   testing; neither is attempted while ForceCPU is on. Back up your
   INI first if you want to keep custom sliders or NPC overrides: the preset
   installs a complete INI. Check that an older INI in MO2's Overwrite or
   another mod is not overriding the newly installed settings.

   Alternatively, edit your effective file without reinstalling:
   Data/SKSE/Plugins/BetterFacialAnimations.ini

   Change these entries in the EXISTING [General] section:
   ForceCPU=1
   UsePerformanceModel=1
   UseOldModel=0
   PotatoMode=1
   SentimentAnalysis=0

   Do not add duplicate entries or put them in Skyrim.ini/SkyrimPrefs.ini.
   In MO2, edit the mod or Overwrite copy that wins for this virtual Data
   path. In Vortex, ensure deployment leaves these values in the game's
   effective INI. Do this with Skyrim closed; its menu saves settings too.

3. Launch through SKSE and load your save. No new save is required just to
   change these settings. Performance reduces inference work; Potato limits
   BFA to your conversation partner and player dialogue. Other speakers use
   vanilla animation. ForceCPU=1 prevents BFA's GPU inference initialization,
   but cannot fix unrelated crashes or every problem elsewhere in the game.

4. No startup recovery file is created or checked. Old gpu-startup.pending
   files are ignored, so an unrelated crash cannot change the provider choice.

If a CPU launch still freezes, keep CPU enabled while investigating the
remaining conflict. If standard independent GPU failed, shared GPU is an
optional next experiment from this working CPU baseline, following the next
page. It is not an automatic fallback. Do not repeatedly retry an unchanged
failing GPU setup hoping the failure will clear.

[Test GPU from a working CPU session]

Force CPU and verify dialogue animates. After updating relevant software,
close Skyrim. To test the other GPU path, edit this entry in the SAME existing
[General] section of BetterFacialAnimations.ini:
IndependentGpuDevice=1  (standard independent device; default)
IndependentGpuDevice=0  (optional 4.0-style shared compatibility device)
Use only one of those values. Changing this route requires a restart; retired
GpuDevice/AutoGpuDevice/UseDeviceWrapper keys are ignored. You can instead
reinstall and choose the route, keeping Force CPU selected.

Keep ForceCPU=1 for the next launch. Load a save and let other mods finish
their startup work. With SKSE Menu Framework installed, open Better Facial
Animations -> Settings -> Model. Select V3 for full detail, or Performance
for less computation, then uncheck Force CPU. This queues GPU initialization
on BFA's worker after current work finishes, using the route chosen before
launch. It does not require reinstalling.

After a returned GPU failure, choose Try GPU again to start another attempt, or
select Force CPU yourself. Switching from CPU to GPU is allowed in the same
session. Shared GPU retries also run automatically; vanilla lip-sync remains
available while no model is loaded. CPU is never selected automatically.
Restart only to change the independent/shared route. Menu settings save
automatically: leaving Force CPU unchecked requests GPU next launch too.
Without the menu framework, edit ForceCPU=0 while Skyrim is closed and relaunch.

Check the actual provider/model status in the menu and log. CPU inference
is not GPU success even if the log lists your graphics card. Startup
logs identify device creation, DirectML, queue creation, ONNX compilation and
warmup. "GPU ready" means warmup returned, not a guarantee of future stability.
A freeze precisely after toggling helps identify a trigger, but does not by
itself distinguish a BFA bug from a driver or graphics-mod interaction.

Common clues:
- 80004002 at independent factory creation: the required interface is absent
  from the runtime/translation layer. Check Windows/Proton support.
- DXGI_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED at independent device creation: the requested path
  is unsupported. Check the complete runtime + driver combination.
- 887A0005: device removed/suspended. This alone does not prove lack of VRAM.
- Missing/wrong ONNX Runtime, DirectML or model: reinstall matching files.


DLSS, frame generation, neural rendering, ReShade, ENB and shader overhauls
can affect the result. For a comparison, hold your save/model fixed and change
one graphics feature at a time using that mod's instructions. A reported DLL
downgrade that helped one NVIDIA setup failed for another; it is not a general
fix. Independent devices separate API state but still share the physical GPU,
driver and Skyrim process. A hung driver call cannot safely be cancelled here.
If GPU startup hangs or crashes, close Skyrim and select Force CPU in the installer or INI.

For a bug report include GPU + CPU, Windows build or SteamOS + Proton version,
driver version, Skyrim/SKSE/BFA versions, model, IndependentGpuDevice and
ForceCPU settings, graphics
mods/upscaler versions, whether a CPU launch works, and the last startup stage.
Attach the full BFA log and crash/freeze log if available. A freeze may leave
no crash log. The usual BFA log location is:
Documents/My Games/Skyrim Special Edition/SKSE/BetterFacialAnimations.log
(Skyrim VR uses its own My Games folder.)

Support and reports:
https://www.nexusmods.com/skyrimspecialedition/mods/193598?tab=posts
https://www.nexusmods.com/skyrimspecialedition/mods/193598?tab=bugs
